text:
In the square outlined by a sparse, poor lawn,
and where everything is proper, flowers, trees,
the panting bourgeois, choking in the heat,
bring their stupidity every Thursday night.

—The military band, in the middle of the garden,
to the Fife Waltz, rocks the shako:
—the dandy displays himself in the front rows
and the notary is nothing but the trinkets hanging from him.


Monocled rentiers underline the mistakes:
puffed-up bureaucrats drag their ladies,
beside whom run, faithful as little dogs,
women in flounces that look like advertisements.


Seated on the benches, retired shopkeepers,
as they prod the sand with their canes,
discuss treaties with great dignity,
snuff silver snuff, and continue: «Well, we were saying!…»


Flattening a plump, flabby back against his bench,
a bourgeois with silver buttons and a northern belly
savors his pipe, from which a strand
of tobacco falls; —You know, I buy it on the black market.


And across the green lawn the young rascals laugh,
while, in love with the sound of the trombone,
innocent, the little bandsmen, sniffing a rose,
caress the child, thinking of the nanny…


I go on, a wreck, just like a student,
beneath the horse chestnut, toward the merry girls:
they know it and turn toward me, laughing,
their eyes curdled with indiscreet ideas.


I do not say a word, but I look at the flesh
of their white, embroidered necks, beneath mad curls:
and I follow the curve, under the light corset,
of a goddess's back, beyond the shoulder's arch.


Soon, like a greyhound, I stalk boots, stockings…
—I reconstruct the bodies and burn in beautiful fevers.
They find me strange and go whispering…
—My brutal desires catch on their lips…

translation.title: To Music
translation.editorial_note: Translated from the stored Spanish rendering, not from Rimbaud's French original. The apparent source corruption 'comacas' is repaired to the evident small-dog comparison, and the colloquial 'turutas' is rendered as little bandsmen; the satire and erotic gaze remain intact.
